messages:
maria: Heads up — I found an old backup tar in s3://redwood-backups/2022-08-21/ named team-configs.tar.gz. Inside there is a file called wrapped_secrets.json with KMS ciphertexts and a small-looking string labelled `vault_token_id`. Not sure if token is live. tagging @eng-security
aj: yikes. can you paste the path and the filename?
maria: s3://redwood-backups/2022-08-21/team-configs.tar.gz -> wrapped_secrets.json
aj: ok. immediate steps: 1) confirm token validity, 2) check KMS key rotation/usage, 3) search audit logs for use of that token or decrypt ops. @samir can you run a search for that `vault_token_id` in vault audit logs?
samir: on it. give me a minute to grep the exported logs. also will check cloudkms decrypt history for the key id embedded in the ciphertext header.
kevin: FYI this backup came from a long-deleted deployment (infra/scripts/old_deploy). it likely contains config scraps. we should assume any token -> compromised until proven otherwise.
maria: I tried a quick validate locally (no decrypt) — the token string looks like a lease id format but truncated. i will not attempt to use it.
aj: good. samir, if logs show token was used after 2022-09-01 we treat it as in-the-wild. otherwise still rotate. also we need to plan KMS key rewrap and Vault token revocation as a precaution.
samir: grep results: no successful vault auth with that token id in the audit logs. cloudkms: there are 3 decrypt ops for key projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/old-ring/cryptoKeys/old-key between 2022-08-22 and 2022-09-10 from serviceAccount:legacy-deploy@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com. No decrypts after 2022-09-10.
aj: that suggests the blob was used during the old deploy window. still treat as sensitive. Next: list current resources that still have IAM bindings to old-key. @kevin can you run `gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy` for that key and check for principals other than legacy-deploy?
kevin: running now. output: principals: legacy-deploy@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com, ops-oncall@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com (viewer), infra-bot@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com (encrypt). I'll paste redacted policy in #eng-infra after.
aj: decision: 1) rotate the KMS key (create new key, grant needed principals, rewrap any ciphertexts we still care about), 2) revoke any Vault tokens that match the pattern (we found token_id but no usage shown), 3) run a scoped search to ensure other backups don't contain plaintext creds. assign: samir -> revoke/check vault; kevin -> KMS IAM tidy + create new key + rewrap plan; maria -> sweep backups and confirm files with ciphertext only; aj -> coordinate and open a security incident ticket with priority P2.
maria: starting backup sweep: I'll run `s3cmd ls` + quick unzip checks for config files and look for strings like "VAULT_TOKEN" or "password". will report count.
vault-bot: automated message: issued command: `vault token-lookup` blocked (no token provided).
samir: for revocation: we can list tokens via Vault operator API if we have token accessor. I'll request an operator token via the secure ops key. if not available we can rotate root policy and re-issue. either way I'll attempt targeted revocation of token_id first.
aj: do not rotate root unless necessary. try targeted revocation. also enable audit log tailing for the next 48h for any use of old-key or that token pattern. samir, after revocation post the curl command you ran (redact actual tokens).
samir: revoked token accessor (redacted) -> responded 204. command used: `curl -s -X PUT $VAULT_ADDR/v1/auth/token/revoke-accessor -d '{"accessor": "REDACTED"}' -H "X-Vault-Token: REDACTED'` (redacted). I also searched leases for related leases id prefix and canceled 2 matching leases.
kevin: KMS plan: create key new-key in same ring, grant encrypt/decrypt to infra-bot and ops-oncall, restrict legacy-deploy SA (it should be removed). I'll create the key and then run `gcloud kms keys versions create` to generate new version. For rewrap: we only need to rewrap active ciphertexts (we found only those 3 decrypt calls). For backups, we'll mark them as scanned and isolated.
aj: timeline: do rotation + revocation within 6 hours, full backup sweep within 24 hours, audit tailing 48 hours. if anything indicates external access, escalate to P1 and notify customers.
maria: backup sweep finished: found 7 archives with wrapped_secrets.json across different dates. all ciphertext-only, no plaintext. I'll move these to a quarantined bucket s3://security-quarantine/2022-backups/ and set object-ACL to private.
kevin: created new-key version v2. IAM updated: removed legacy-deploy SA, infra-bot + ops-oncall kept. rewrap run for the three ciphertexts that were still referenced by internal metadata: success. steps logged in ops-runbook ticket.
samir: vault revocation done and confirmed via `vault token-lookup` (accessor returns 404). Also rotated the lease secret backends that referenced the old tokens (i.e., job-runner roles).
aj: please post the incident ticket link here once created. also run a quick grep across our public repos for the filename `wrapped_secrets.json` — if it's in any public repo we need immediate takedown.
kevin: grep across github org: no matches in public. several matches in archived private repos (which we scanned).
maria: small action item: update backup retention policy to run a secret-scan on backups older than 30d and auto-quarantine matches. I'll draft a short PR to infra with the scan step.
aj: good. final checklist: - tokens revoked (samir) - KMS key rotated/rewrapped (kevin) - backups quarantined and scanned (maria) - audit tailing on for 48h (aj) - incident ticket open (aj) - communicate to partners if partner svcacc had access (kevin to check)
ops-oncall: alert channel muted for this thread.
maria: partner check: legacy key was never granted to external partner accounts. confirmed.
aj: closing note: no evidence of external compromise; actions completed. we'll leave audit tailing and retention PR in review. reopen if any new logs show activity. :thumbsup:
